plain_language_meaning: Abbreviation for person under investigation. A person with particular disease symptoms, but who is not confirmed to have the disease.
Giant full-body suits and helmets healthcare workers wear to treat people quarantined with infectious diseases.
Able to make others sick; spreadable; a disease that can be spread from one person to another; someone who is sick and might make you sick too.
A measure to protect those at highest risk of severe illness if they catch COVID-19 (or any other infectious germ) by minimising all interaction between them and others.
The amount of space between two places, people or things.
News, facts, or knowledge about a situation, person, event that are correct, exact, and without any mistakes.
Any acute decline in lung function of sudden onset, whether traumatic or related to disease state; may be life threatening.

An alcohol-containing preparation (liquid, gel or foam) designed for application to the hands to inactivate microorganisms and/or temporarily suppress their growth. Such preparations may contain one or more types of alcohol, other active ingredients with excipients, and humectants.
The plural of alveolus. The alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs where the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place.
Anything that destroys bacteria or suppresses their growth or their ability to reproduce. Heat, chemicals such as chlorine, and antibiotic drugs all have antibacterial properties.
Medicine; drug that fights bacteria; infection-fighting medicine.
Able to destroy harmful microbes (small living things that can cause disease).
Drugs that are effective against a retroviruses, like HIV for example.
The parts of the body that air passes through during the act of breathing, consisting of the mouth, nose, throat, and lungs.
Someone who is sick but does not feel or look sick.
The use of drugs, exercises, etc. to cure a person of an illness or injury.
A place where medical care given to a patient for an illness or injury.
To keep someone or something safe from injury, damage, or loss.
The condition or state of being kept safe from injury, damage, or loss.
Poisonous or not pure.
Affected with a disease-causing and harmful organism.
A person who has a particular disease confirmed usually by a laboratory test.
A strong chemical used for cleaning things or removing colour from things.
The system that moves blood throughout the body. The circulatory system is composed of the heart, arteries, capillaries, and veins.
Life support system that circulates the blood through an oxygenating system. ECMO is like a heart-lung machine that takes over the work of the heart and lungs during open heart surgery.

Abbreviation for the Center for Disease Control and Prevention. CDC is one of the major operating components of the US Department of Health and Human Services. It is responsible for controlling the introduction and spread of infectious diseases (in the United States), and provides consultation and assistance to other nations and international agencies to assist in improving their disease prevention and control, environmental health, and health promotion activities.
An infectious disease caused by a newly discovered coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2).
Abbreviation for computed tomography scan. Special x-ray test that shows inside body parts.
An acutely disturbed state of mind characterized by restlessness, illusions, and incoherence, occurring in intoxication, fever, and other disorders.
A description of a patient's illness including symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.
An illness in which the body's solid waste is more liquid than usual and comes out of the body more often.
A rapid expulsion of air from the lungs not accompanied by phlegm production.
A small drop, such as a particle of moisture discharged from the mouth during coughing, sneezing, or speaking; these may transmit infections while airborne to others.

Abbreviation for severe acute respiratory syndrome. An infectious disease with symptoms including fever and cough and in some cases progressing to pneumonia and respiratory failure. It is caused by a coronavirus named SARS-CoV.

Abbreviation for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. It is a life support system that circulates the blood through an oxygenating system. ECMO is like a heart-lung machine that takes over the work of the heart and lungs during open heart surgery.
Referring to a product that can be used once and is then thrown away.
A substance produced by a living organism which acts as a catalyst to bring about a specific biochemical reaction.
The occurrence of more cases of a disease than would be expected in a community or region during a given time period.
The study of how infectious diseases spread, occur, and are controlled.
An acute respiratory infection with history of fever or measured fever of ≥ 38 C°, and cough, with onset within the last 10 days, and requires hospitalization.
An infectious disease with symptoms including fever and cough and in some cases progressing to pneumonia and respiratory failure. It is caused by a coronavirus named SARS-CoV.
Keeping physical space (distance) between yourself and other people outside of your home in order to reduce the spread of an infectious disease like COVID-19.

The process of working collaboratively with and through groups of people affiliated by geographic proximity, special interest, or similar situations to address issues affecting the well-being of those people.
Occurs when a virus is being passed from person to person in a community and starts appearing in people who aren’t known to have contact with an infected person.

Information or statements of opinion about something provided by the people living in one particular area or people who are considered as a unit because of their common interests, social group, or nationality.
Readiness, alertness, to be ready, to be prepared, to be planned.
A currently circulating story or report of uncertain or doubtful truth.

A covering made of fibre or gauze and fitting over the nose and mouth to prevent you from breathing in harmful substances, such as bacteria or pollution, or from breathing bacteria or viruses onto anyone else.
News, facts, or knowledge about the condition of someone's body or mind; or about medical activities.
People working in the provision of health services, whether as individual practitioners or employees of health institutions and programs.
The set of services or activities provided for the treatment of the physically and the mentally ill.
A person engaged in actions whose primary intent is to enhance health.
A person who has the particular disease, health disorder, or condition which meets the case definition for surveillance and outbreak investigation purposes.
The number of people who have died from a disease divided by the number of people who got that disease.
A highly contagious viral infection of the respiratory passages causing fever, severe aching, and excessive mucous, and often occurring in epidemics. Formal name for flu is "influenza".
A highly contagious viral infection of the respiratory passages causing fever, severe aching, and excessive mucous, and often occurring in epidemics.
A liquid-like substance used for cleaning your hands and killing bacteria on them.

A general term referring to any action of hand cleansing. Hand hygiene includes: applying an alcohol-based hand rub to the surface of hands and washing hands with the use of a water and soap or a soap solution, either non-antimicrobial or antimicrobial. When performed correctly, hand hygiene results in a reduction of microorganisms on hands.
A liquid-like substance used for cleaning your hands and killing bacteria on them.
Cleaning one's hands.
A liquid-like substance used for cleaning your hands and killing bacteria on them.
The practice or principles of keeping yourself and your environment clean to maintain health and prevent disease.
An act of forcing air out of your lungs through your throat with a short, loud sound, often unwillingly.
A place where people who are ill or injured are treated and taken care of by doctors and nurses.

People with immune systems that are (usually artificially) weakened. People with organ transplants take immunosuppressants to stop their immune systems from attacking the organs. Immunosuppressed people are also immunocompromised.
Out of the body, outside the body, laboratory grown, in a test tube.
Within the body, inside the body, grown inside animal.
The process or an act of giving someone a vaccine (a substance put into a person's body to prevent them getting a disease).
Illness caused by germs; a sickness you get from germs.
Infection prevention and control (IPC) is a scientific approach and practical solution designed to prevent harm caused by infection to patients and health workers.
Policies and procedures used to minimize the risk of spreading infections, especially in hospitals and human or animal health care facilities.
Action, treatment, program.
The amount of time it takes for an infected person to start showing symptoms.
Facts about a situation, person, event, etc.
A situation in which people are not allowed to enter or leave a building or area freely because of an emergency.
A part of a hospital that provides continuous treatment for patients who are seriously ill, very badly injured, or who have just had an operation.
Abbreviation for intensive care unit. It is a part of a hospital that provides continuous treatment for patients who are seriously ill, very badly injured, or who have just had an operation.
The condition of being separated from other people, towns, countries, etc.
A thin tube inserted into a vein or body cavity to administer medication, drain off fluid, or insert a surgical instrument.
The testing of a person or group of people for the presence of a disease or other condition.
A very small organism that causes disease.
Relating to the observation and treatment of actual patients rather than theoretical or laboratory studies.
A study that is intended to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of medications or medical devices by monitoring their effects on large groups of people.
The practice of identifying and monitoring individuals who may have had contact with an infectious person as a means of controlling the spread of a communicable disease.
A medical condition in which the body temperature is higher than usual and the heart beats very fast.
A family of viruses that cause illnesses in animals and humans, including COVID-19
The feeling of not getting enough air when you are breathing.
Extremely serious or dangerous disease of the body or mind.
A period of time during which an animal or person that might have a disease is kept away from other people or animals so that the disease cannot spread.
Lung infection.
To manage the rate or quantity of something (for example infections) so that it does not increase too much within a short period of time.
Relating to medicine or to the treatment of illness or injury.
Personal protective equipment that covers the mouth and nose of the wearer to prevent the spreading of respiratory viruses and bacteria.
The provision of what is necessary for a person's health and well-being by a doctor, nurse, or other healthcare professional.
A substance, especially in the form of a liquid or a pill, that is a treatment for illness or injury.
A process of using a mechanical ventilator to help a patient breathe (ventilate) when he or she cannot breathe on his or her own for any reason (for example during a surgery or a critical illness).

Abbreviation for Middle East respiratory syndrome. It is an infectious disease with initial symptoms including fever and cough and progressing in a fairly high proportion of cases to pneumonia and respiratory failure. It is caused by a coronavirus.
A commonly believed but false idea.

The feeling of not getting enough air into your lungs; shortness of breath; labored breathing. It is a sign of a variety of disorders and is primarily an indication of inadequate ventilation or of insufficient amounts of oxygen in the circulating blood.
Relating to newborn children (or other mammals).
An intensive care unit designed for premature and ill newborn babies.
To make a sudden involuntary expulsion of air from the nose and mouth due to irritation of one's nostrils.
Abbreviation for neonatal intensive care unit. It is an intensive care unit designed for premature and ill newborn babies.
Relating to a serious, unexpected, and often dangerous situation requiring immediate action.
Something that causes death.
Chronic or long-term health related issues that can weaken the immune system. For example: asthma, diabetes, heart problems etc.
To clean something using chemicals that kill bacteria and other very small living things that cause disease.
A substance that contains chemicals that kill bacteria and is used especially for cleaning surfaces in bathrooms and kitchens.
Drugs that can be bought without a prescription.
The spread of disease. A disease can be transmitted from person to person, from person to animal to person or by the environment.
A virus that has just started to exist or has just been discovered, affecting breathing system and causing respiratory illness.
Being able to offer more services in an emergency, ability to expand
People of a similar age or within a particular range of ages.
Persons aged 65 years and over.
A disease existing in almost all of an area or in almost all of a group of people, animals, or plants. It causes a large number of deaths
A person receiving or registered to receive medical treatment.
A bacteria, microbe, parasite, fungus, virus or other organism that causes a disease.
An estimate of the amount of oxygen in the blood.

A person who does not have particular disease symptoms but who has been in contact with someone who is presumed or confirmed to have the disease. A PUM is “monitored” until they’ve gone a period of time without developing symptoms.
A person with particular disease symptoms, but who is not confirmed to have the disease.
Clothing and other equipment such as masks and gloves that is worn or used to protect people against infection or injury.
The term local transmission means that the source of the infection has been identified within the reporting location (such as within a country, region or city).

A method of ventilation in which airway pressure is maintained above atmospheric pressure at the end of exhalation by means of a mechanical impedance, usually a valve, within the circuit. The purpose of PEEP is to increase the volume of gas remaining in the lungs at the end of expiration in order to decrease the shunting of blood through the lungs and improve gas exchange.

Abbreviation for person under monitoring. A person who does not have particular disease symptoms but who has been in contact with someone who is presumed or confirmed to have the disease. A PUM is “monitored” until they’ve gone a period of time without developing symptoms.
Abbreviation for personal protective equipment. Clothing and other equipment such as masks and gloves that is worn or used to protect people against infection or injury.
Medical treatment provided by local/family doctors or other health workers, rather than special treatment in a hospital.
Method, standard, step-by-step process, way of doing things, rules, code.
A reaction to something.
A device that forces air into a person’s lungs when the person cannot breathe independently and needs help to breathe
Relating to breathing (respiration).
A disease affecting your breathing system (respiratory tract) caused by a virus or bacteria.
An inability of the lungs to perform their basic task of gas exchange (the transfer of oxygen from inhaled air into the blood and the transfer of carbon dioxide from the blood into exhaled air).
A labored breathing, characterized by an inappropriate degree of effort to breathe based on rate, rhythm, and subjective evaluation of respiratory effort.
Life-threatening condition where the lungs can't provide the body's vital organs with enough oxygen.

A disease that impacts lungs, throat and airways. Respiratory illnesses primarily cause coughing, fever and can lead to severe pneumonia. Most are spread in respiratory droplets, which are virus-filled drops of water we shoot out when we cough and sneeze. Although respiratory illnesses attack airways, they can ultimately damage a number of other organs.
A virus causing a disease that impacts lungs, throat and airways.
The possibility that something bad or dangerous will happen.

The exchange of real-time information, advice and opinions between experts and people facing threats to their health, economic or social well-being. The ultimate purpose of risk communication is to enable people at risk to take informed decisions to protect themselves and their loved ones.
Abbreviation for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. It is the official name of the virus causing the COVID-19 disease.
A substance used for washing the body or other things.
A condition in which the throat is red and painful, especially during swallowing
A period of time when you keep yourself away from other people if you think you may have a disease in order to prevent the disease from spreading

It is responsible for controlling the introduction and spread of infectious diseases (in the United States), and provides consultation and assistance to other nations and international agencies to assist in improving their disease prevention and control, environmental health, and health promotion activities.
A situation when schools have stopped operating.
Relating to the observation and treatment of actual patients rather than theoretical or laboratory studies.

The exchange of real-time information, advice and opinions between experts and people facing threats to their health, economic or social well-being. The ultimate purpose of risk communication is to enable people at risk to take informed decisions to protect themselves and their loved ones.
Preexisting conditions are health conditions someone already has and that could make an infection or another illness worse. Lung disease, asthma and heart disease are preexisting conditions.
Chronic or long-term health related issues that can weaken the immune system. For example: asthma, diabetes, heart problems etc.
A situation in which people are not allowed to enter or leave a building or area freely because of an emergency.
Able to make others sick; spreadable; a disease that can be spread from one person to another; someone who is sick and might make you sick too.

To (cause to) cover, reach, or have an effect on a wider or increasing area.

A liquid-like substance used for cleaning your hands and killing bacteria on them.

When performed correctly, hand hygiene results in a reduction of microorganisms on hands.
A liquid-like substance used for cleaning your hands and killing bacteria on them.

An immune system that isn’t functioning correctly. You can be immunocompromised by diseases like AIDS or taking some anti-cancer drugs, but you can also be immunocompromised by losing sleep, not drinking enough water and eating poorly.

A disease affecting your breathing system (respiratory tract) caused by a virus or bacteria.

To stop something from happening.
Stop, bar, avoid
